about:
# CraftColors

> **CraftColors is now part of [EverlookDB Crafting](https://github.com/quikmn/EverlookDBCrafting)** (`/ecraft colors`,
> the "Profession window" page): the same colours, skill-up chance and counts, and your CraftColors settings are
> carried over. With EverlookDB Crafting enabled, CraftColors stands down by itself and you can disable it. This
> repository gets no new features.

WoW Forever (interface 16001). Colors recipe names in the profession window by skill-up difficulty: orange, yellow, green, gray. Works in the profession window (Enchanting included) and, should the game open one, the older-style trade skill and craft windows.

![The Tailoring window with recipe names colored by difficulty: orange, yellow, green and gray](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/quikmn/CraftColors/main/media/screenshot.png)
![Further down the same list: gloves, belts and leggings, each colored by difficulty](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/quikmn/CraftColors/main/media/screenshot-2.png)
![The Enchanting window: rods, oils and chest enchants colored by difficulty](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/quikmn/CraftColors/main/media/screenshot-3.png)

## Commands

`/ccolors` (also `/craftcolors`) follows the same pattern as every EverlookDB addon:

- `/ccolors` opens the settings window: colouring on or off, your own colour for each difficulty, how much the row under the mouse brightens. It's also under Settings > AddOns.
- `/ccolors off`, `/ccolors on` (or `toggle`): the colouring.
- `/ccolors orange ff8040` (or `yellow`, `green`, `gray`, `hover 0.3`), or `/ccolors set orange ff8040`: change a setting; `/ccolors get` lists them.
- `/ccolors debug` prints what the game says about the selected recipe (handy for bug reports; `/ccolors check` still works).
- `/ccolors reset` puts the colours back (type it twice within 10 seconds).
- `/ccolors search <words>` opens the window with its search box filled; `/ccolors status`, `/ccolors version`.
- `/ccolors feedback` shows a link for reporting bugs and ideas. `/ccolors help` (or `?`) lists every command; a mistyped one suggests the nearest.

## Install
WowUp: pick **World of Warcraft: Forever**, then Get Addons → Install from URL, and paste `https://github.com/quikmn/CraftColors`.

By hand: download the latest zip from Releases and unzip it into `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns`.

releases.notes:
- CraftColors is now part of EverlookDB Crafting (`/ecraft colors`), and your settings carry over. With EverlookDB Crafting enabled, CraftColors steps aside and you can disable it. This is CraftColors' last version.
- Fixed: the skill-up % and count no longer overlap long recipe names or repeat the game's own count.

- After each yellow and green recipe: your chance of a skill-up ("37%"). Needs EverlookDB Crafting; without it the names are only coloured.
- After each recipe: how many you can make from your bags ("(4)"), optionally with your bank and other characters ("(4 +5)").

- Softer settings window colours and clearer switches.
- The recipe check moved out of the settings window to `/ccolors debug`.
- Turning the colours off no longer leaves a recipe stuck in its mouse-over colour.
- Recipe names are also coloured in the older-style trade skill and craft windows.

- Settings: an AI help button copies a description of every setting for an AI assistant, and `/ccolors apply` runs the commands it gives back.
- Chat commands now follow one pattern across all EverlookDB addons: `/ccolors help` (or `?`) lists them. New short name `/ccolors` (`/craftcolors` still works); `/ccolors on`, `off` and `toggle` for the colouring; `get` and `set <setting> <value>`; `search <words>`; `status` and `version`; `/ccolors reset` asks first (type it again within 10 seconds); a mistyped command suggests the nearest one.
- The settings window has a search box at the top: type to find any setting.

- `/craftcolors` opens a settings window: turn the colouring off, pick your own colour for each difficulty, how much the row under the mouse brightens, and what the game says about the selected recipe. CraftColors also has an entry in the game's Settings > AddOns that opens it. Every setting works from chat too (`/craftcolors orange ff8040`, `/craftcolors settings`, `/craftcolors help`). The old recipe check is `/craftcolors check`; the feedback link opens in CraftColors' own small window.
- `/craftcolors feedback` shows a link for reporting bugs and ideas.
- Turning "Colour recipe names" off now puts the game's own colours back right away.
- Settings window: Escape closes an open dropdown list first, then the window; Escape in a text box puts the old text back; a number typed next to a slider snaps to the slider's steps; a Delete or Reset that asks for a second click no longer forgets it early.
